q: Which law's IRR sets the minimum size of an accessible elevator car?
o: BP 344 (Accessibility Law)
PD 1096 (National Building Code)
RA 9514 (Fire Code)
RA 11285 (Energy Efficiency Act)
ref: BP 344 Revised IRR (2024), Appendix A
n: The BP 344 IRR, revised in 2024, sets the accessible car at 1,400 mm deep by 1,200 mm wide, with a 900 mm door.

q: Under the Green Building Code, what is elevator standby operation for?
o: Parking the cars at the top floor
Cutting energy use during off-peak periods
Shortening the door-closing time
Raising the car speed at peak hours
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015) — escalators, moving walks and elevators
n: During low traffic, idle cars shut down lights, fans and drives until called.

q: Which pair of measures does the Green Building Code call for?
o: Hydraulic drives for all elevators and full-speed escalators
Two-speed AC motors and escalators on timers only
VVVF drives for traction elevators and sensor controls for escalators
DC motor-generator sets and escalators started by hand
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015) — escalators, moving walks and elevators
n: AC variable-voltage variable-frequency drives are required on non-hydraulic elevators. Escalators and walks must slow down and go to standby when idle.

q: Under the BP 344 IRR, what must be provided with an escalator in a transport facility?
o: A freight elevator as the only alternative
A second escalator going the same way
Nothing more, as long as signs are posted
A signed alternative pedestrian route nearby
ref: BP 344 Revised IRR (2024), Appendix A
n: People who cannot ride an escalator need another way up, such as an elevator or ramp, close by and signed.

q: Which approach reduces ventilation fan energy when full airflow is not always needed?
o: Demand-based control with variable-speed fans
Running every fan at full speed around the clock
Closing all outdoor-air intakes to save energy
Oversizing the fans so they run less often
ref: ASHRAE 62.1 terminology; Grondzik and Kwok, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings
n: Sensors lower airflow when fewer people are present. Fan power falls roughly with the cube of speed.

q: What escalator controls does the Green Building Code require?
o: Run at full speed whenever the building is open
Slow down after 1½ minutes and go to standby after 5 minutes with no traffic
Stop only when switched off by a guard
Slow down after 10 minutes and stop after 30 minutes
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015) — escalators, moving walks and elevators
n: Sensors at the landings detect riders. The 1½- and 5-minute limits are maximums and may be adjusted to demand.

q: What does the Green Building Code require of elevator car lighting when the car is idle?
o: It stays on around the clock for safety
It switches off after 30 minutes of no use
It switches off after at most 5 minutes of no use
It dims only when the building is closed
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015) — escalators, moving walks and elevators
n: Car lights must also be efficient, averaging over 55 lumens per watt.

q: How does the Green Building Code want moving walks to start and stop?
o: Started and stopped by hand by the guard
At full speed at all times, for safety
By a clock timer set by the building owner
Soft-start drives triggered by landing sensors
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015) — escalators, moving walks and elevators
n: Soft starts avoid jerks and current spikes, and landing sensors switch the walk between standby, slow and full speed.

q: Under the BP 344 IRR, what is the minimum accessible elevator car size in transport facilities such as train stations?
o: 1,400 mm deep × 1,500 mm wide
1,400 mm deep × 1,200 mm wide
1,100 mm deep × 1,400 mm wide
1,200 mm deep × 1,200 mm wide
ref: BP 344 Revised IRR (2024), Appendix A, Sec. 5.6 and C.8.5
n: Transport facilities get the larger 1,400 × 1,500 mm car. In other buildings the minimum is 1,400 mm deep by 1,200 mm wide. Both need a 900 mm door.

q: Under the BP 344 IRR, what is the maximum angle of inclination of an escalator?
ref: BP 344 Revised IRR (2024), Appendix A, Sec. 10.3
n: The 2024 IRR limits escalators to 30°, with at least three flat steps at each end for people with limited mobility.

q: For an accessible route between floors, which element gives independent access where stairs cannot?
o: Escalator
Stair with handrails on both sides
Accessible elevator
Inclined moving walk steeper than 12°
ref: BP 344 Revised IRR (2024), Appendix A
n: An elevator is the preferred vertical access under BP 344. Escalators and stairs cannot be used by wheelchair users.

q: Under the BP 344 IRR, how far at most may an accessible elevator be from the building entrance?
ref: BP 344 Revised IRR (2024), Appendix A, Sec. 8.4
n: Accessible elevators must be within 30 m of the entrance and signed. Large transport facilities that cannot meet this provide respite areas.

q: Which elevator-car lighting meets the Green Building Code?
o: Efficient lamps averaging over 55 lm/W, off after 5 minutes idle
Incandescent lamps kept on for passenger comfort
Fluorescent lamps switched off after 30 minutes idle
Any lamp at all, as long as it is dimmable
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015) — escalators, moving walks and elevators
n: The code sets both an efficacy floor for car and display lighting and an idle switch-off time.

q: An architect provides only an escalator between two public levels where an accessible route is required. What is wrong?
o: Nothing, since escalators can carry wheelchairs
An escalator alone does not give an accessible route
The escalator must be replaced by a stair
Only the handrail height needs checking
ref: BP 344 Revised IRR (2024), Appendix A
n: Wheelchair users cannot ride escalators. An accessible elevator, ramp or lift must also be provided.

q: Under the BP 344 IRR, when several adjoining escalators are installed, what is required?
o: All must run upward in the morning
All must run the same direction
At least one going up and one going down
Only one may run at a time
ref: BP 344 Revised IRR (2024), Appendix A
n: A dedicated down escalator must pair with the up one, unless users never travel both ways at once.

q: Which drive does the Green Building Code call for on non-hydraulic elevators?
o: Two-speed AC drive
Hydraulic pump drive
DC motor-generator (Ward Leonard) drive
AC variable-voltage variable-frequency (VVVF) drive
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015) — escalators, moving walks and elevators
n: VVVF drives control motor speed smoothly and can regenerate power, using far less energy than older drives.

q: Why is soft-start technology useful for escalators?
o: It ramps the motor up gently, cutting current and wear
It lets the escalator run with no motor at all
It widens the steps at the landings for carts
It keeps the escalator at full speed at all times
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015) — escalators, moving walks and elevators
n: Escalators that stop and start often under sensor control need soft starts to avoid jerking riders and stressing the drive.

q: Under the BP 344 IRR, what is the minimum clear door opening of an accessible elevator?
o: 900 mm
800 mm
700 mm
ref: BP 344 Revised IRR (2024), Appendix A
n: The accessible elevator door must give at least 900 mm clear, the same as other accessible doors.

q: What is no-traffic detection on moving walks for?
o: Keeping the walk at full speed for safety
Counting passengers for billing
Cutting energy use during idle periods
Detecting fires on the walkway
ref: Philippine Green Building Code (2015) — escalators, moving walks and elevators
n: When sensors see no riders, the walk slows and then stops on standby.

q: Why does an accessible elevator need a wide clear door?
o: It lets the car carry larger freight
It shortens the door-closing time
It reduces the hoistway depth
Wheelchair users need room to pass through and turn
ref: BP 344 Revised IRR (2024), Appendix A
n: A 900 mm clear opening lets a wheelchair pass. The 1,800 × 1,800 mm lobby gives room to turn.
